question: Can the published metric be reproduced under the same physical and evaluation model?
audience: Researchers assessing decoder failure across noise conditions
baseline: Closest-integer gate decoding and conventional rotated surface-code resource comparison

settings.outer_decoder: dynamic matching edge weights using complete analog history and space-time correlations
settings.rare_event_policy: For zero failures report confidence upper bound, never claim zero logical error.

hypothesis: The registered metric can be matched under the original protocol; no predicted advantage in the qkp simulator is asserted.
decision_rule: Compare independently measured estimates and uncertainty with reported values or marked visual-reading ranges. A match is provisional until model, split and units are audited; missing code/data or imprecise estimates remain inconclusive. Do not tune on held-out test data.
compute: Smoke: CPU, one thread, small bounded input. Production: explicitly launch after resolving listed blockers; no full training is started by fetch/check.
uncertainty: Wilson intervals for independent Bernoulli counts; bootstrap trajectory/seed-level fits for lifetimes and thresholds. Use three independent training seeds for new training, reported separately.
procedure: First reproduce the joint two-mode CNOT displacement decoder against closest-integer rounding at 12 dB. Then implement the Appendix C memory circuit with dynamically weighted, correlated matching graphs and perform the squeezing sweep. Preserve the paper’s variance-to-dB convention and count both relevant gate failure components.
blockers: No verified public author simulation repository located.
Full correlated gate model and dynamically weighted matching implementation remain to be implemented from the paper appendices.
A 1e-7 failure claim requires adequate rare-event statistics, not a smoke run.
raw_output_contract: See ../RESULTS.md. Save raw outcomes, checkpoint/config/source hashes, environment, seed and noise units.
